8. A copy of the minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors held on 11th August, 1985 is also annexed as Annexure-37 which shows that the petitioner No. 1 received a sum of Tk. 6,10,000.00 from the respondent No. 1 on different dates. Annexure-40 is the letter allegedly written by Mr. RN Chakraborty, Chief Accountant, which shows that Mr. RN Chakraborty offered Tk.25,000.00 to the petitioner at his residence on 8.10.86 which he refused. Annexure-41 is dated 22nd January, 1985 from which it appears that the Deputy Chief Manager of Pubali Bank wrote to the Assistant Chief Manager of Pubali Bank, Local Office, Dhaka about the release of the property of the petitioner No. 1 mortgaged to the Pubali Bank. Annexure-42 is the Bank Guarantee dated 2.3.85 given by the National Bank Ltd. for an amount of Tk. 25 lacs to the Pubali Bank on behalf of the respondent No. 2 company. 

 9. Annexure-43 is a letter from the respondent No. 1 to the Managing Director, Pubali Bank Ltd., Head Office, Dhaka. This is dated 14th January, 1987. By this letter the respondent No. 1 requested the Managing Director to release the properties of the petitioner No. 1. Annexure-44 is the letter dated 5.2.87 which was written by the Deputy Chief Manager, Pubali Bank, Head Office, to the respondent No. 1 stating that the bank was not in a position to consider his request for release of the security of Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed, ex-director, till full payment of the settled amount of the company with the Local Office, Dhaka. Annexure-45 is the alleged draft copy of the agreement allegedly vetted by the Legal Adviser of the respondent No. 2. 

 12. As regards the aforesaid mortgage of the petitioner No.1, Deputy Manager, Pubali Bank, wrote a letter on 22.3.90 regarding the liability of M/s Paper Converting and Packaging Ltd. On 2.4.90 the Deputy Manager, Pubali Bank, issued a certificate with the heading: 

 22. In this sentence the word “মধ্যেই” is very relevant and significant for the purpose of the present case. It appears that the respondent No.1 had given such an undertaking or taken such a responsibility that he must get the mortgaged house and press released from the Pubali Bank in favour of the petitioner No.1 by 31.3.86. There is no proviso or any other clause in the agreement by which or for which a lenient or different interpretation can be given to this undertaking which the respondent No.1 had taken and given. Now I am to consider whether the respondent No.1 acted in accordance with the terms of the contract and whether he had ever fulfilled the terms of his undertaking given in the agreement. In the affidavit-in-opposition, Annexure-41 is dated 22nd January, 1985. This IS a letter from the Deputy General Manager of the Head Office of Pubali Bank to the Assistant General Manager, Local Office of the Pubali Bank. This relates to the release of collateral securities of the properties mortgaged by Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed in favour of M/s. Paper Converting and Packaging Ltd. It is not very relevant as it was a correspondence made prior to the date of agreement. Annexure-42 to the affidavit-in-opposition is the Bank Guarantee of Tk. 25 lacs given by the National Bank Ltd. in favour of the company which was given to the Pubali Bank. It is also dated 2nd March, 1985 whereas the agreement was made on 8.3.85. So, this Bank Guarantee was also given before the date of agreement. Annexure-43 of the affidavit-in-opposition is dated 14th January, 1987. This is the letter written by the Managing Director, Pubali Bank Ltd., Head Office, Dhaka. The respondent No.1 stated that since he had purchased all shares of Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed and his sons and wife, he had undertaken all- the liabilities of Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed including those relating to Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, ICB, Pubali Bank, Ltd. which also included Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed's personal security which was offered and given in the interest of the company. In the event of any fresh undertaking if needed to cover the liabilities of Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed, Mr. Lutfur Rahman (respondent No. 1) agreed to do so. In view of the above, it is so cited that Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed may please be relieved from all his liabilities including his personal security offered in the interest of the bank. This letter was written on January 14, 1987, whereas a deadline of releasing the mortgaged property from Pubali Bank expired on 31st March, 1986. Obviously, it appears from the record that respondent No.1 failed to fulfill the second term of the agreement by not getting the house and the press released in favour of Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed by 31st March, 1986. 

 24. Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, submits that as regards payment of Tk.10 lacs, since the petitioner No.1 refused to take the money the respondent No.1 was unable to pay it. This submission of Mr. Ishtiaq Ahmed has not been substantiated by any paper on record. Rather the paper namely, the letter of Mr. RN Chakraborty, the Chief Accountant, dated 14.10.86 clearly shows that Tk.25,000.00 was offered after the last date of payment of installment as the last date was 30.7.86. Petitioner No. 1. and respondent No.1 are full brothers. Money was to be paid by the respondent No.1 to the Petitioner No.1 as per terms of the agreement. It is difficult to understand why Mr. RN Chakraborty was dragged in this matter of payment of money to the petitioner No.1. Respondent No.1 could have issued a cheque or bank draft in favour of the petitioner No.1 and sent it by registered post. If it was refused, then such a contention could be given some weight. Further, it could not be shown that by the last date i.e. 30.7.86 the respondent No.1 offered the remaining amount of Tk. 10 lacs to the petitioner No.1, because the alleged offer of Tk. 25,000.00 does not fulfill the terms of the agreement. Since the respondent No.1 failed to fulfill his own obligation as per terms of the agreement, he is not entitled to get any benefit out of it. 

 "The Chief Baron read the later part of section 35. I cannot imagine any language better adopted for conferring a jurisdiction to decide disputes between two alleged members of a company in respect of the title to shares therein. I think, therefore, that the jurisdiction exists."
